How Daily Interest Works

1. Starting Principal Calculation
NAF = Finance Amount + All Financed Fees
Commission = NAF × Commission Rate
Starting Principal = NAF + Commission (fully capitalised)

Unlike monthly compounding, daily interest lenders typically provide a single "starting principal" figure that already includes everything.

2. Daily Interest Calculation
Daily Rate = Annual Rate ÷ 365
Interest Per Period = Balance × Daily Rate × Actual Days
First Payment = Settlement day counts as day 1 (+1 day interest)

Interest varies each month based on actual calendar days. A 31-day month accrues more interest than a 28-day month.

3. Payment Date Adjustments
If payment falls on weekend → Move to next Monday
If payment falls on NSW public holiday → Move to next business day
Target payment day maintained month-to-month where possible

This calculator uses NSW public holidays as Autopay/MoneyMe is Sydney-based. Toggle above to enable/disable this adjustment.

NSW Public Holidays included (2025-2030): New Year's Day, Australia Day, Good Friday, Easter Saturday, Easter Monday, Anzac Day, Queen's Birthday (2nd Mon June), Bank Holiday (1st Mon Aug), Labour Day (1st Mon Oct), Christmas Day, Boxing Day. When holidays fall on weekends, substitute days are observed on the next available weekday.

4. Why Daily Interest Matters
Daily Rate: 0.0245% per day
30-day month interest: $0.00
31-day month interest: $0.00

The variable interest means amortization schedules from daily-interest lenders won't match monthly-compounding calculators exactly.
